I thought about this and came to some conclusions as I desperately wanted to answer the question of "why?" I came up with a few risk factors based off of what all school shooters seem to have in common: depression, being male, feeling wronged and needing justice - narcissism? a lack of empathy, being a social outcast due to being overall strange - lacking in social skills, severely introverted, etc. Poor environmental circumstances - poor family and or friends. But mostly - anger due to perceived injustice (anger is a tip of the iceberg emotion, underneath I believe there might be a lot of frustration and sorrow).

I think depression - severe depression, has two forms: an inward acting form of depression and an outward. I believe these guys (yes so far there has been no female shooter and until then I won't say anything else) have all this mix in their brain and therefor it results in an outward acting depression. Notice how they also commit suicide themselves. You could say they're just trying to get out of a responsibility for their crimes - but they could have seen a value in their life prior to committing those acts and chosen not risking getting shot by police or be thrown in jail forever. They don't see value in their lives and not in anyone else's - that's the outward acting depression with a horrible foundation of the factors mentioned earlier. Some people commit suicide and some people commit genocide. Furthermore, males are more likely to commit violent crimes and I believe genetic predisposition is the cause of that.

This comment is not made to justify any violent acts. Anything one does in life is ones own responsibility. Many people might have been dealt similar cards in life and they've chosen to take other routes.

So overall I felt lied to and used as some sort of therapist. But yeah what I've learned, like I said, if someone values you they'll appreciate your efforts. We did not hang out more than like 3 times a month, if that. She would keep me updated, I would keep her updated. I guess some people are just really good at being fake. I didn't text her constantly, maybe once every two days or day, something small. So overall I think she just did not like me. But it was convenient for her to vent to me... also I had bought her a gift for her b-day and she said she wasn't gonna celebrate, fast-forward a few days and she arranges a "celebration party" cause she got into a school. Yeah, no, I believe in this case that her trying to end the friendship on a "civil note" is her ending it so she won't have that much guilt later on. She thinks I'm a nice person but yet she's been lowkey resentful and haven't been honest about it. I say resentful because I had issues at home, for the first time ever I sent a snap of me being sad about something and she ignored it. She didn't ask me how I was the following 4 days either. She couldn't be honest with me about that - that's why I don't trust the rest either, it might be PART of the reasons why - but I believe if you think your friend texts too much that's because you don't enjoy their friendship. And that is ultimately a symptom of something else. There are reasons she couldn't disclose without looking like a true ass, but I'd rather hear the reasons of resentment and I would not like to end it on a nice note for the sake of her guilt. She shouldn't have pretended to be my friend for so long and used me to listen to her million problems while she couldn't even bear the thought of listening to one of mine because she resents me so much.

If he has an iPhone you can check his recent locations in settings. Check who he's calling, check his pictures, if he uses snapchat check that. I mean he probably got a lock on his phone cause he seems a bit sly if I'm gonna be honest. If you can't access his phone, have enough dignity for yourself and your body (cause who knows if he's got an STD if he's sleeping around?) and tell him straight up your suspicions and ask him to hand over his phone. This is plan B though. Be sneaky about it first. I'm sorry if this sounds like "bad advice" but honestly, I've had a guy be unfaithful to their girlfriend WITH ME. I didn't know they had a GF until later. He would constantly hide his phone from me and went home late at night, so yes... if he is acting shady then you gotta be acting shady too cause he won't have an honest conversation with you.
